subject: Interlock: liability cap vs SLA credits — ACME order form
messages:
From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme FinTech Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME redlines — liability cap / SLA remedy question

Rishi — attaching our redlines to the MSA and the order form. Two quick items Procurement wants clarified before legal routing: 1) We see Redwood proposes a broad limitation of liability capped at fees paid in prior 12 months; Procurement is asking that SLA service credits be treated as an offset to amounts payable (i.e., credits reduce Redwood's liability). 2) They want an explicit carve-out for consequential damages for some categories but not for data security incidents.

We flagged the proposed "credits as sole remedy" language as well — they don't like a clause that would bar them from recovering damages after credits if there's a material business impact. Can you confirm Redwood's position so I can take to my legal?

Attachments: ACME_MSA_redlines_v2.pdf (annotated), ACME_OrderForm_Redline_stub.pdf

Thanks,
Jared Liu
Head of Procurement, Acme FinTech

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME redlines — liability cap / SLA remedy question

Jared — thanks for the redlines and the clear note. High level position from Redwood: we are prepared to stand behind an industry-standard limitation of liability (fees paid in prior 12 months) with the usual carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, and indemnity obligations (IP infringement, third-party claims).

On SLA credits vs. cap: our preferred model is that service credits are the exclusive remedy for SLA failures (i.e., they do not give rise to additional monetary damages) and that credits are NOT counted as an offset against the contractual liability cap. The rationale: credits are a measured, contractual remedy tied to the operational failure and are deliberately narrow; allowing double recovery (credits + damages) undermines the economics that let us offer predictable pricing.

That said, we are open to a compromise for larger customers — e.g., credits remain the sole remedy for typical availability/performance incidents, but an exception exists for data incidents or willful misconduct where the cap is lifted (or increased).

Looping in Neha and Laura to propose precise clause language we can send back to Acme.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME redlines — liability cap / SLA remedy question

Thanks for the context. Drafting guidance from Legal: we should present Acme with a clean, defensible position and one concessionary path. Suggested approach:

1) Limitation of Liability clause: Cap is the greater of (a) fees paid in the 12 months prior to the claim or (b) $500,000 (we can pick a numeric floor to help negotiation) — carve-outs for willful misconduct, gross negligence, breach of confidentiality, indemnity obligations, and violation of data security obligations (where cap does not apply).

2) SLA / Service Credits clause: Service credits will be the sole and exclusive contractual remedy for availability/performance SLA failures (provide credits schedule). Credits shall not be treated as damages for purposes of the limitation of liability.

3) Exception language: For Security Incidents resulting in unauthorized data access or exfiltration, the liability cap does not apply and Customer reserves other remedies.

4) Optional commercial compromise: offer that, for this order form only, Redwood will increase the liability cap to 12 months fees + an additional amount equal to three times the monthly recurring fees for certain categories — but only if Acme agrees that credits remain the exclusive remedy for standard SLA misses.

I can draft specific redline text for the MSA and the Order Form. Any preference on numeric floor or multiplier? Proposed floor: $500k; proposed multiplier: 3x monthly recurring fee for targeted carve-out.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME redlines — liability cap / SLA remedy question

Rishi / Neha — negotiating note from commercial: Acme is strategic for our payments integrations and they have expansion upside. I'd prioritize getting Order Form signed with a pragmatic compromise rather than holding to a hard no. My suggested negotiation posture to Jared:

- Keep credits as the sole remedy for performance/availability incidents; explicitly state credits are not damages and do not reduce the liability cap.
- For data/security incidents, carve out the cap entirely.
- To give Acme comfort on operational risk, offer a higher cap for this customer: "Cap equals fees paid in prior 12 months, with a floor of $500k; for claims arising from SLA failures, Redwood's aggregate liability shall not exceed fees paid in prior 12 months, but Redwood will provide a one-time increased cap equal to (fees paid in prior 12 months + 3x MRR) if the failure relates to platform availability impacting payment processing for more than 48 consecutive hours."

That last bullet is a commercial hedge — gives Acme a path to higher recovery for a catastrophic outage that affects their core payment flows, while keeping most outages limited to credits. If Legal can provide redline text that captures this without too much ambiguity, I'm OK moving forward.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
laura@redwood.com

From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme FinTech Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 14:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME redlines — liability cap / SLA remedy question

Rishi — appreciate the quick engagement and the proposed compromises. A couple of points from our side after discussion with Legal/Engineering:

- We can accept that typical SLA credits are the exclusive remedy for standard availability issues, provided there is a meaningful credits schedule (we're proposing a maximum single-month credit equal to 100% of monthly fees for a P1 outage) and an annual cap (e.g., 3x MRR) on credits.
- However, we need to preserve the right to seek monetary damages (subject to the overall cap) for incidents that cause business interruption even if credits are paid — we will not agree to language that treats credits as a substitute for all claims arising from consequences to our customers.

If Redwood insists that credits never count against the liability cap, that will be a hard stop for Procurement. Would Redwood be willing to accept a middle ground: credits are the exclusive remedy for most SLA misses and do not immediately reduce the cap, BUT if there is a consequential business loss demonstrably beyond what credits compensate for (e.g., chargebacks caused by prolonged downtime), credits may be reflected in the calculation of amounts recoverable up to the stated cap? That preserves the concept of sole remedy for normal outages but lets us pursue excess economic harm in extreme cases.

We prefer to see the final redline language you propose.

Best,
Jared

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: ACME — proposed final redline for liability / credits (please review)

Team — per the thread and the commercial ask, I prepared a consolidated redline to send to ACME. Key points included in the attached redlined MSA and Order Form:

1) Limitation of Liability: Redwood's aggregate liability for all claims arising from or related to the Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, or (b) $500,000; provided, however, that the foregoing limitation shall not apply to (i) damages arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) Redwood's indemnification obligations for third-party IP claims, or (iii) a Security Incident involving unauthorized access to or exfiltration of Customer Data (in which case the liability cap shall not apply).

2) SLA / Service Credits: For validated availability or performance breaches, Customer's exclusive contractual remedy shall be service credits as set forth in the SLA schedule. Service credits shall not be treated as monetary damages for the purposes of calculating Redwood's liability cap. Service credits shall be capped per incident and annually (SLA schedule attached).

3) Catastrophic outage carve-out: For outages that (a) impact Acme's core payment processing for more than forty-eight (48) consecutive hours and (b) cause demonstrable customer-facing chargebacks or regulatory reporting obligations, Redwood agrees to a one-time increased liability remedy equal to (fees in prior 12 months + 3x MRR) for claims directly attributable to that outage. This carve-out is intended to address Jared's concern about consequential business interruption while preserving credit-only remedies for ordinary SLA misses.

4) Negotiation note: we are *not* proposing that credits be a dollar-for-dollar offset that automatically erodes the general liability cap. However, Legal may permit limited reconciliation language so that, in the specifically defined catastrophic scenario above, recoverable amounts may be computed net of previously issued credits to avoid double recovery.

Please review the attached redlines (ACME_MSA_redlines_v2.pdf and ACME_OrderForm_Redline_stub.pdf). If Legal signs off on the wording above I will circulate to Jared for final confirmation and DocuSign routing.

Action requested: Neha — can you confirm final legal sign-off or suggest edits to the proposed carve-outs/phrasing by end-of-day Friday? Laura / Marissa — any commercial tweaks?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
